content.title: USMNT falls to Portugal 2-0 to end March international break ahead of World Cup
content.text: The U.S. men's national team will end March 0-2. In the second and final friendly of this international break, the U.S. took on Portugal in Atlanta and fell 2-0, a result that comes off the heels of a 5-2 loss to Belgium on Saturday. After that eye-opening loss, head coach Mauricio Pochettino made several changes to the starting 11. Christian Pulisic was deployed as a false nine, while Tim Weah moved up from right-back to right wing with Alex Freeman slotting in. Chris Richards and Auston Trusty formed the center-back partnership with Matt Freese coming back in as GK1 for Matt Turner. Grinding out a win was always going to be difficult considering Portugal is a serious contender for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Cristiano Ronaldo was not involved in this break. The changes to the lineup included a visible lack of chemistry. In the 36th minute, Portugal made the U.S. pay. After winning the ball back, a splitting pass in between Richards and Trusty into Bruno Fernandes led to a clever back heel, which right winger Francisco Trincao slotted home. The U.S. had been proactive on the ball up to that point, but didn't create enough serious damage to land a blow first. Instead, one mistake resulted in a concession the other way. It's been a recurring theme for the team with not enough quality defenders. Portugal added a second just before the hour mark, doing so on a well-worked set piece. And it was Fernandes once again with the assist, something he's done often this season with Manchester United. MORE SOCCER COVERAGE From the left corner, Fernandes picked out Joao Felix, who stood on the edge of the box. He controlled the ball well before exquisitely picking out the far left bottom corner himself. Freese could not reach it in time. That would be it from a scoring perspective, as Pochettino also made three changes at halftime. Pulisic was replaced for Patrick Agyemang, who scored late vs. Belgium and was rewarded with a full half. Antonee Robinson and Weston McKennie, two likely starters at the World Cup, came off for Max Arfsten and Tanner Tessman, as well. The expected goals were quite low, as Portugal just edged it 0.74 to 0.68, per FotMob. But the two strikes were the difference in quality when it comes to taking half-chances. Portugal had 62% possession to go with 11 shots, with five on target. The U.S. shot 12 times, with only three on target against Jose Sa, who is not the nation's first-choice goalie (Diogo Costa). Neither team generated a big chance. The result for the U.S. means it has lost eight straight games to European opposition. It is winless in its last 10 dating back to 2021, being outscored 22-6. Pulisic is also without a national-team goal since November 2024, a streak of eight games. His body language as a false nine in the first half suggested a man desperate for a taste of the net again. He also hasn't scored for AC Milan in 12 games, dating back to late December 2025. Pochettino and Co. now have until the end of May for their next games before the World Cup gets underway in mid-June. First up is a friendly against Senegal on May 31. Senegal is a sleeper dark horse for the World Cup and getting a win will be extremely difficult with the nation's pace-and-power and technical quality. Then the U.S. will meet Germany on June 6 in a World Cup send-off match. The DFB are a known powerhouse and are expected to contend for the title, though their ceiling will ultimately be foreshadowed by Julian Nagelsmann's chosen squad. If the USMNT's stat line in March are anything to go by, going into the tournament with poor results and performances will not lead to the desired run it so desperately needs. 15:52Why the FIFA World Cup reigns supreme to all other sporting events Roger Bennett previewed his new book “We Are The World (Cup),” talked about on his favorite World Cup memories and predicted the world champion.
